text:
maria: Heads up — competitor announced a feature called AdaptiveRouting that auto-selects model variants by latency/cost. Got 3 enterprise asks last week to match a per-route fallback/degeneration feature. Need to decide whether to push this into the next sprint or keep it as a later differentiator. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

alex: Quick clarifying q — are customers asking for routing semantics (auto-fallback) or for visibility (per-route billing/metrics)?

devon: Sales: primarily routing + SLA alignment. They want automatic fallback to a smaller model under load, plus a way to pin routes to a capacity tier. Also asked for canary for fallback rules.

sam: Design: UX complexity = medium. We can do a simple toggle in the Console for "fallback: on/off" and an advanced JSON policy editor for power users. Will need good defaults.

lia: Research: we already have a prototype for model-variant families in the lab branch. Perf/regret numbers are reasonable — ~10–15% quality drop with cost savings ~35–45% on short prompts. Worth validating on a couple of customer workloads.

jordan: Product POV: propose splitting into two scoped deliveries: (A) API/runtime primitives for fallback and a default safe policy (MVP) (B) Console UX, rollout visuals, and per-route observability (stretch). We should define launch criteria for MVP so sales can commit to customers.

maria: Proposal: MVP in the next release focused on API behavior + safe default policy; Console and A/B tooling in the following release. Draft acceptance criteria below:

```text
MVP Acceptance:
- API: support a `fallback_policy` route parameter (simple schema)
- Runtime: automated model fallback must occur within 200ms of overload detection
- Quality: no more than 2% increase in error/invalid responses when fallback triggers
- Tests: E2E with 3 model families + perf bench across seq lengths
```

alex: Eng notes: need updates to routing layer + kernel selection mapping for model variants. Can reuse current KV cache code but we must handle cache invalidation across quantized variants — risk area. Rough estimate: 3 sprints with 2 engineers to first-cut.

devon: Messaging: we can position this as "predictable degradation + cost control". If we have concrete cost delta numbers for typical workloads, marketing / account execs will love it.

maria: Decision: Approve MVP scope as proposed. Stretch items (console visualizations, advanced policy editor, A/B testing) move to follow-up milestone. Action items: alex -> tech spec by Tue, sam -> mockups by Wed, lia -> perf validation matrix and customer sim.

jordan: I'll block 30m Thu for scope sync and to prioritize backlog. @devon please bring two customer examples we can run the perf sims against.

launchbot: Reminder: RFC required before merging major runtime changes. Please add the tech spec to the RFC tracker and link the runbook once ready.
